story.headline: A Win at Georgetown, Then Heartbreakers
story.text: Seniors Corny Thompson and Mike McKay led one more fast start. UConn won 14 of its first 17 games, none bigger than a 63–52 win at No. 13 Georgetown on January 20, 1982, against a Hoyas team, featuring freshman Patrick Ewing, that would reach the national championship game. Three days later the Huskies edged Villanova 53–51 in Hartford. Then the close games turned against them: UConn lost eight of its last 11, including a 61–59 loss at Seton Hall and an overtime loss at Villanova, and finished 7–7 in the Big East. With the Big East tournament at the Hartford Civic Center, the Huskies lost 54–52 to St. John's in the quarterfinals, and the season ended with a 76–75 overtime loss at Dayton in the first round of the NIT. Thompson made first-team All-Big East for the second straight year and McKay second team; Thompson finished with 1,810 points and 1,017 rebounds, McKay with 1,633 points. Their four teams went 78–37, and Thompson, Chuck Aleksinas and McKay were all chosen in the 1982 NBA draft.

moments.title: Win at Georgetown
moments.text: UConn beats No. 13 Georgetown 63–52 on the road; the Hoyas, with freshman Patrick Ewing, would reach the national final.

moments.title: Big East tournament in Hartford
moments.text: St. John's edges UConn 54–52 in the Big East quarterfinals at the Hartford Civic Center.

moments.title: NIT First Round: L at Dayton
moments.text: Dayton beats UConn 76–75 in overtime in the first round of the NIT.
